chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Is'haq ibn Ghalib, from Al Husayn ibn Mihran, from Abdullah ibn Usman, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who worsens his manners, punishes his own self.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of having bad manners according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that poor character is not merely a social flaw but a mechanism of self-torment, reflecting the Shia concept of *adab* as the foundation of spiritual health. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the intrinsic link between ethical conduct and inner peace, suggesting that moral decay inevitably leads to psychological and spiritual distress. It serves as a practical reminder for believers to cultivate noble traits to avoid the self-inflicted punishment of a troubled soul.
